NASA's 2022 mission to intentionally crash a spacecraft into the asteroid Dimorphos has been followed by the arrival of Europe's Hera probe, which will analyze the impact site and assess the effectiveness of such a planetary defense method. The Hera mission aims to gather data on the asteroid's internal structure and the consequences of the collision, which successfully altered Dimorphos' orbit around a larger asteroid, Didymos. This research is crucial for determining the feasibility of using kinetic impacts to redirect potentially threatening asteroids in the future.

 - NASA's DART mission successfully changed the orbit of the asteroid Dimorphos by crashing into it at high speed.
 - The European Space Agency's Hera probe has now arrived to study the impacts and gather data for future planetary defense.

Source: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/science/space/nasa-deliberately-crashed-a-spacecraft-into-an-asteroid-in-2022-europes-hera-probe-has-now-reached-the-impact-site-to-measure-how-successfully-humanity-can-deflect-a-space-rock/articleshow/135792858.cms

Vision-language models like CLIP are designed to classify images into categories without explicit training for those categories, but accuracy decreases when the test images differ from the training images. The current dominant method for improving accuracy relies on prediction entropy to identify trustworthy views of images, but new research shows that this method is inadequate. An alternative approach that considers the fraction of the original image retained by each crop has been found to improve accuracy significantly across multiple benchmark datasets.

 - Vision-language models can classify unseen categories, but their accuracy decreases with style differences in test images.
 - Current methods using prediction entropy for view selection are shown to be ineffective, with new methods demonstrating improved accuracy.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14686

Machine unlearning allows owners of large language models to remove specific entities from their models without complete retraining. New research identifies a security threat known as the Proxy Unlearning Attack, where legitimate requests to unlearn can inadvertently remove sensitive information due to overlapping representations within the model. A proposed solution involves Superposition-Aware Unlearning Protection, which aims to safeguard sensitive data while executing unlearning tasks.

 - Machine unlearning can potentially compromise sensitive knowledge due to knowledge superposition in large language models.
 - The Proxy Unlearning Attack presents a security vulnerability where legitimate unlearning requests can delete unintended sensitive entities.
 - A defense mechanism called Superposition-Aware Unlearning Protection is proposed to mitigate the risks associated with unlearning sensitive knowledge.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15013

To address this, a defense framework called Superposition-Aware Unlearning Protection (SAUP) has been proposed to safeguard against these vulnerabilities.

 - Machine unlearning allows for the removal of specific entities from trained models without needing to retrain them from scratch.
 - The new threat posed by Proxy Unlearning Attacks (PUA) can unintentionally result in the removal of sensitive entities that were not targeted.

A new efficient polynomial-time approximation scheme (EPTAS) for the Max-Cut problem on interval graphs has been developed, providing significant improvements over previous approximation ratios. The algorithm is deterministic and utilizes a structural theorem that transforms interval graphs, ensuring efficiency in finding approximate cuts for unweighted graphs. The study also confirms the NP-hard status of approximating Max-Cut on chordal graphs, which intersects with interval graphs.

 - A new deterministic efficient polynomial-time approximation scheme (EPTAS) for Max-Cut on interval graphs has been introduced.

 - The algorithm's implementation utilizes a structural theorem to enhance approximation efficiency.
